title: Streaming + Tools Docs: Messaging Review (Hosted API) — Terminology, Guarantees, and Deprecations
content:
Owner: Nikhil (PM, Hosted API)
Doc purpose: PM-led messaging review for the DevEx “streaming + tool calling + structured output” examples/docs refresh. This is not a protocol spec. Goal is user-facing clarity, consistent terminology, and safe/accurate promises.
Last review pass: 2025-02-18 (terminology sign-off + deprecation language)

---

1) Background / why this doc exists
We’re updating developer-facing docs + SDK examples to reduce support load and improve time-to-first-success for agentic workflows.
Top confusion themes (from Support + SE):
- Users expect “OpenAI-like” semantics but hit small payload shape / naming differences.
- Users treat tool-call args as complete JSON at every stream step; parse errors / truncated args (SUP-18421).
- Users assume “structured output” means “always valid JSON” across all models; not universally true (SUP-18436).
- Docs mix terms: “JSON mode”, “schema constrained”, “structured outputs”, “function calling”, “tools”.

This review sets the words we use, what we promise, what we explicitly don’t promise, and how we talk about deprecations/migrations.

Non-goals:
- Do not rename the underlying API fields for this refresh.
- Do not introduce new guarantees not backed by model/runtime behavior.

---

2) Audience + doc tone
Primary: software engineers + ML engineers integrating Redwood API (Hosted), often via SDK.
Secondary: platform engineers evaluating Dedicated/Private.
Tone: practical, production-first. Prefer “here’s the stable pattern; here are pitfalls and recovery strategies”.
Avoid aspirational claims like “always” / “guaranteed” unless we can enforce across models.

---

3) Canonical terms (use these consistently)

3.1 Streaming
Use: “streaming responses” or “response streaming”.
Avoid: “SSE mode” as the headline term (ok as implementation detail).
Definition for docs:
- Streaming delivers incremental events (“deltas”) as the model produces output.
- The SDK assembles deltas into a final assistant message.
- Tool calls may appear mid-stream.

Required callout box (“Streaming mental model”):
- Deltas are partial; do not assume each chunk is valid JSON.
- Final assembled message (or tool call) is the reliable unit to parse/validate.

3.2 Tool calling
Use: “tool calling” (primary). Allow “function calling” as a parenthetical only in compatibility contexts.
Definition:
- You provide a list of tool definitions (name + description + JSON schema for arguments).
- The model may respond with a tool call (tool name + arguments).
- Your app executes the tool and sends a tool-result message back.

Key language choice:
- Prefer “tool definitions” (not “functions” in Redwood-native docs).
- Prefer “tool result message” (not “function response”).

3.3 Structured output
Use: “structured output” (primary).
Subtitle/clarifier (first mention on page): “structured output (JSON schema-constrained)”.
Avoid: “JSON mode” as a primary phrase; too OpenAI-coded and implies hard guarantees.
Definition:
- You ask the model to output JSON that conforms to a provided JSON Schema.
- Your application should validate (and optionally retry) if output is invalid.

3.4 Compatibility references
Use: “OpenAI-compatible API surface” (if applicable) and “compat differences” section.
Avoid framing any differences as “bugs”; say “differences in payload shape and event naming”.

---

4) Claims & guarantees: what we can safely say

4.1 Streaming guarantees (safe)
Say:
- “Streaming provides incremental events and a final completion event.”
- “Deltas may contain partial tokens; assemble the final message before parsing.”
- “Tool call arguments may arrive in multiple chunks; treat arguments as an incremental buffer until the tool call is complete.”

Do NOT say:
- “Every chunk is valid JSON.”
- “Tool call args are always complete in the first event.”

4.2 Tool calling guarantees (safe)
Say:
- “Tool calling is model-dependent; Redwood will route and serve your selected model, but tool-call behavior varies by model family.”
- “You should validate tool arguments against your schema before execution.”
- “Parallel tool calls are supported in the canonical examples; your application must collect and respond with a tool-result message for each tool call.”

Do NOT say:
- “The model will always call tools when it should.”
- “Tool arguments are always valid / always match schema.”

4.3 Structured output guarantees (safe)
Say:
- “Schema-constrained output improves reliability but is not a substitute for validation.”
- “Validate the final response against your JSON Schema and implement a repair/retry strategy.”
- “Some models provide stronger adherence than others; see the model support matrix.”

Do NOT say:
- “Guaranteed valid JSON.”
- “Guaranteed schema compliance.”

---

5) Required sections on the docs pages

5.1 “Known pitfalls” section (must exist on tool calling + structured output pages)
Include at minimum:
- Partial tool-call arguments during streaming (SUP-18421): buffer and wait for completion; validate after assembly.
- Incremental JSON parse errors (SUP-18436): validate final; if streaming UI wants partial JSON, display raw text and only parse at end.
- Retry semantics: network disconnects can interrupt streams; re-issue request with idempotency key / app-level retry; be explicit about duplications.
- Strict vs permissive parsing: use strict JSON parsing at the end; during stream, do not parse.

5.2 “Compatibility notes” section
Short, non-defensive.
- “If you’ve used OpenAI tool calling before, note that field names / event types may differ. See compatibility notes for details.”
- Link to compat doc (redwood-openai-compat PR reference).

5.3 “When to use what” decision table
A small table helps reduce confusion:
- Tool calling: when you need external actions (search, DB, tickets, etc.).
- Structured output: when you need JSON in a stable shape (extract entities, config objects, forms).
- Both: agent plans a tool call, then outputs a structured summary.

---

6) Deprecation + migration language (template)
We need a consistent approach because docs changes will surface “old snippet shape” and older SDK versions.

6.1 Principles
- Deprecate examples and docs patterns, not the API, unless we are truly deprecating an endpoint.
- Always state “since SDK vX.Y.Z” (or “requires SDK >= …”) for copy/paste snippets.
- Provide a short “If you’re on older versions” callout with the minimal differences.

6.2 Suggested wording blocks

A) Soft deprecation (docs pattern only)
“Note: Older examples may show <old pattern>. That pattern still works, but we recommend the updated approach below for more reliable streaming and tool-call handling (partial arguments, retries, and validation).”

B) Hard deprecation (API behavior changing)
“Deprecated: <feature> will be removed on <date>. New integrations should use <new feature>. Existing users must migrate by <date> to avoid breaking changes.”
(Only use if we have an actual removal date + comms plan.)

C) Version gating
“This example requires redwood-sdk-<lang> >= <version>.”
“If you are pinned to an older SDK: <one bullet list of differences> + link.”

6.3 What we should deprecate in this refresh
- Any docs implying chunk-by-chunk JSON parsing is supported/recommended.
- Any tool calling examples that omit schema validation and tool-result message loop.
- Any streaming examples that do not show final assembly and error handling.

---

7) Copy changes to apply across docs (editorial rules)

7.1 Replace “function calling” → “tool calling”
Allowed exceptions:
- “tool calling (also known as function calling)” in the first paragraph.
- Compatibility section headings.

7.2 Replace “JSON mode” → “structured output”
Add: “structured output (JSON schema-constrained)” on first mention.

7.3 Avoid absolute language
Replace:
- “guaranteed” → “aims to”, “designed to”, “improves”, “typically”.
- “always valid JSON” → “validate final JSON; retry on invalid output”.

7.4 Make the failure path explicit
Every structured output snippet should show:
- validate
- if invalid: either (a) retry with a repair prompt, or (b) fall back to non-structured text and log an alert

---

8) Proposed messaging for each guide (draft text)

8.1 Streaming guide intro (draft)
“Streaming responses let you start rendering output immediately while the model is generating. Redwood streams incremental deltas and a final assembled message. Because streamed chunks are partial by nature, buffer the deltas and only parse structured data (tool arguments, JSON output) once the final content is complete.”

8.2 Tool calling guide intro (draft)
“Tool calling lets your model request actions from your application. You define tools with JSON schemas for arguments; the model can emit a tool call; your application executes the tool and returns a tool-result message. Tool-call arguments may stream in multiple chunks—validate arguments after assembly before executing.”

8.3 Structured output guide intro (draft)
“Structured output helps you get JSON in a predictable shape using a JSON Schema. Because model output can still be malformed, always validate the final response and implement a retry/repair strategy for production workflows.”

---

9) Open questions / decisions needed (as of last modified)
- Model support matrix (PM-413): We need a public-facing matrix that is honest without overwhelming. Proposal: categorize as ‘strong’, ‘partial’, ‘best-effort’ for (a) tool calling and (b) structured output. Owners: Henry + Applied ML input. Blocker for final copy.
- How prominently to surface compat differences: suggestion is a short “Compatibility notes” callout with a link (don’t derail the main flow).
- Whether to mention “parallel tool calls” as default: recommend yes, but keep the first example single-tool for clarity; add second example for parallel.

---

10) Action items
- Wei (Docs): apply terminology changes + remove “JSON mode” from headings (keep as parenthetical once).
- Ibrahim (SDK parity): ensure examples match the language used here (tool definitions, tool-result messages, final assembly).
- Support (Dev / Priya): review known pitfalls list and confirm it matches top ticket drivers; add 1–2 concrete ‘symptom → cause → fix’ bullets.
- Nikhil (PM): finalize model support matrix wording and approve the final deprecation callouts.

---

Appendix A: Support-driven “symptom → fix” snippets (for Known Pitfalls)
1) Symptom: Tool call args look truncated / JSON parse fails mid-stream.
Cause: Arguments are streaming incrementally; you’re parsing before the tool call is complete.
Fix: Buffer argument chunks; parse/validate after final tool call event; treat partial args as plain text until complete.

2) Symptom: Structured output occasionally emits invalid JSON.
Cause: Model adherence varies; streaming truncation; schema too permissive/too strict; or prompt conflict.
Fix: Validate final output; retry with repair prompt (“Return ONLY valid JSON matching this schema…”); log invalid outputs; consider a more adherence-friendly model per the support matrix.

Appendix B: Copy checklist (quick)
- [ ] Uses “tool calling” not “function calling” (except compat)
- [ ] Uses “structured output (JSON schema-constrained)” on first mention
- [ ] No claims of guaranteed JSON/schema compliance
- [ ] Streaming page explicitly says: assemble first, parse later
- [ ] Examples show validation + failure handling
- [ ] Version gating included for SDK snippets
